title: Q (worked examples): Atomic Number, Mass Number & Isotopes
notes: **Q1. For the atom ₁₂Mg²⁴, find the number of protons, electrons and neutrons.** Atomic number Z = 12, so protons = 12 and electrons = 12 (neutral atom). Mass number A = 24, so neutrons = A − Z = 24 − 12 = 12.

**Q2. The magnesium ion Mg²⁺ has atomic number 12. How many protons and electrons does it contain?** Protons = Z = 12 (unchanged). Since the ion has lost 2 electrons, electrons = 12 − 2 = 10. Its atomic number remains 12.

**Q3. Protium (₁H¹), deuterium (₁H²) and tritium (₁H³) are isotopes. How do they differ?** All three have the same atomic number Z = 1 (one proton and one electron) but different mass numbers. Protium has 0 neutrons, deuterium has 1 neutron, and tritium has 2 neutrons. Protium is most abundant (99.98%), deuterium about 0.015%, and tritium only 10⁻¹⁵ % (radioactive).

**Q4. Show that ₁₈Ar⁴⁰, ₁₉K⁴⁰ and ₂₀Ca⁴⁰ are isobars.** All three atoms have the same mass number A = 40 but different atomic numbers (18, 19, 20). Hence they are isobars — atoms of different elements with the same mass number.

**Q5. Show that ₆C¹⁴, ₇N¹⁵ and ₈O¹⁶ are isotones.** For ₆C¹⁴: neutrons = 14 − 6 = 8. For ₇N¹⁵: neutrons = 15 − 7 = 8. For ₈O¹⁶: neutrons = 16 − 8 = 8. All have the same number of neutrons (8) but different atomic and mass numbers, hence they are isotones.

**Q6. Verify that ₁₉K³⁹ and ₉F¹⁹ are isodiaphers.** For ₁₉K³⁹: neutrons − protons = (39 − 19) − 19 = 20 − 19 = 1. For ₉F¹⁹: neutrons − protons = (19 − 9) − 9 = 10 − 9 = 1. Both have the same isotopic excess (1), hence they are isodiaphers.
